Japanese Marine sentry interfering with
S.M. Police on duty.

At 5.30 p.m. 1/3/41 a telephone message was
received from C.P.C. 219 reporting that C.P.C. 1224 was
having trouble with a Japanese marine sentry at the N.
Kiangse and Range Roads barrier.

At 6 p.m. 1/3/41 C.P.C. 1224 appeared at the
Charge Room and from subsequent enquiries made the fo-
llowing was ascertained:-

C.P.C. 1224 was, at 3 p.m. 1/3/41 detailed
for duty at the North Kiangse and Range Roads barrier,
where the Japanese Marines maintain a double sentry
post.

At about 5.30 p.m. 1/3/41 C.P.C. 1224 was
standing on the west side of the barrier near to the
opening, when he observed one of the sentries stop
and search a hawker who intended to enter the West
Hongkew district from the Hongkew side.

This hawker was carrying two baskets suspended
from a bamboo pole.

Whether the sentry found something or not in
the possession of the hawker is not known to the C.P.C.
but the sentry roughly handled him, the hawker, tied
his hands with string and made him stand near to the
sentry box, which is situated on the Hongkew side of the
barbed wire.

1941年3月1日下午3时，中央巡捕房1224号警员被派往江西路北路与兰路路障处执勤，该处由日本海军陆战队设有双岗哨位。

1941年3月1日下午5时30分左右，中央巡捕房1224号警员正站在路障开口处西侧，此时他目睹其中一名哨兵拦停并搜查一名意图从虹口一侧进入西虹口区的摊贩。

该摊贩肩挑一根竹竿，两端各挂一只篮子。

中央巡捕房警员并不知晓哨兵是否在摊贩身上搜出物品，但哨兵粗暴对待该摊贩，用绳子捆绑其双手，并令其站在位于铁丝网虹口一侧的哨兵岗亭旁。

C.P.C.1224 did not interfere but continued to
perform his duty. About ten minutes later the sentry
approached him and speaking in Chinese asked if he had
seen the hawker who it appears had disappeared.
He gave a negative answer and commenced to
walk away and the sentry returned to his post.
About five minutes later C.P.C.1224 had occasion
to stop a truck loaded with rice which was about to
pass through the barrier into the Hongkew Area.
The object of stopping this vehicle was to
ascertain whether they had the necessary permit.
Whether the halting of this vehicle caused some
annoyance to the sentry is not quite clear, but
directly same had passed, the same sentry who had
arrested the hawker again approached C.P.C.1224,
caught hold of his cross belt and pulled him to the
Hongkew side of the barrier and told him to stand by
the sentry box, at the same time informing him that
he would be taken to Japanese Military Headquarters
where he would be assaulted.
Whilst the sentry was engaged in searching
pedestrians, C.P.C.1224 managed to return to the
West Hongkew side of the barrier.
Statement of C.P.C.1224 attached.

中央巡捕房1224号警员未加干涉，继续履行职责。约十分钟后，该哨兵走近他，用中文询问是否见过那名似乎已消失的摊贩。
他予以否认，并开始走开，哨兵则返回其岗位。
约五分钟后，中央巡捕房1224号警员因故拦停一辆装载大米、正准备穿过路障进入虹口区域的卡车。
拦停该车辆的目的是查验其是否持有必要的通行证。
尚不完全清楚拦停该车辆是否引起哨兵的某种恼怒，但在该车通过后，此前逮捕摊贩的同一名哨兵再次走近中央巡捕房1224号警员，抓住他的斜跨皮带，将他拉至路障的虹口一侧，并命令他站在哨兵岗亭旁，同时告知他将被带往日本军事总部，并将在那里遭到殴打。
趁哨兵忙于搜查行人之际，中央巡捕房1224号警员设法返回路障的西虹口一侧。
附中央巡捕房1224号警员陈述书。

at the Japanese Military Headquarters, North Railway

C.P.C.1254 arrived on the scene, interfered

Enquiries at the scene failed to secure any

The C.P.C. stoutly denies the allegations of the

日本海军陆战队哨兵声称，他在路障处拦停了两辆装载大米的卡车，在检查其通行证后允许其通行。
中央巡捕房1254号警员（原文如此）到达现场，进行干涉并强迫司机下车，一名身份不明的日本平民告知哨兵，该警官正向卡车司机索取“好处费”（squeeze）。这导致哨兵抓住了该中央巡捕房警员。
在现场的调查未能找到任何证人，涉事机动车亦不明。
该中央巡捕房警员坚决否认哨兵的指控，并完全驳斥其对事件经过的描述。

W.H'kew Stn.        1/./41.        -------- Clerk Chao.

I reported for duty at 3 p.m. 1 /41 and
was detailed to North Kiangse Road near Rnage Road.
At about 5.30 p.m. I saw a Japanese sentry on duty
at the opening of the barbed wire barricade on the above roads.
catch hold of a second hand hawker and order him to stand by
the side of the sentry box. After a while the arrested hawker
disappeared, and the Japanese sentry in question approached
me and asked me if I had seen in which direction the hawker
had gone, to which I replied in the negative. The sentry
then returned to his post. After which I went about 50 yds.
from the opening of the barricade and saw a m/truck approaching
from W. to E. and stopped the vehicle and asked the driver
of the car if he had rice transportation permit which after
being examined was allowed to proceed into the Hongkew Area.
About 5 minutes after this, the said sentry again
approached me and grasped hold of me and took me to the
side of is sentry box and told me to stand there. Following
which, he told me that I would be taken to the Japanese Head-
quarters and there beaten.
Being afraid that I might be beaten by the Japanese,
I took the advantage of the time when the said sentry was
searching passers by, I ran away from the place.
The above is my true statement.

Signed by:-
C.P.C.1224.

西虹口巡捕房        1941年..月..日        -------- 赵书记员（Clerk Chao）。

我于1941年1月下午3时报到执勤，
被派往江西路北路靠近兰路（Rnage Road，原文拼写错误）处。
下午5时30分左右，我看见一名日本哨兵在上述道路的铁丝网路障开口处执勤。
他抓住一名二手货摊贩，命令其站在哨兵岗亭旁。过了一会儿，被捕的摊贩消失了，前述日本哨兵走近我，问我是否看见摊贩朝哪个方向走了，我回答没看见。随后哨兵返回其岗位。之后我走到距离路障开口约50码处，看见一辆机动车从西向东驶来，我便拦停该车辆，询问司机是否有大米运输许可证，经查证后允许其进入虹口区。
此后约5分钟，该哨兵再次走近我，抓住我并将我带到他的哨兵岗亭旁，命令我站在那里。接着，他告诉我，我将被带往日本总部，并在那里挨打。
因害怕被日本人殴打，我趁该哨兵搜查路人之际，从现场逃离。
以上是我的真实陈述。

签署人：
中央巡捕房1224号警员。

Sir,

S. M.C. came to the Station together with C. Cs. 411

disarmed and taken away by two male Japanese dressed

    At 2.45 a.m. 17.2.41, C. Cs. 411 and 531 were on
duty at 3 Post at Ichang Road Bridge. Suddenly they
heard sounds of people shouting on Gordon Road and upon
investigating, they discovered a motor car, Naval Landing

the motor car reached the C.P.Cs., two male Japanese
alighted and started to speak to the Policemen in the
Japanese language. The two Japanese, both of whom were
dressed in the uniform of the Japanese Naval Landing
Party, appeared to be in an excited condition and after
talking for a few seconds, suddenly assaulted the two
C. P. Cs about the face and head with the butt ends of the
pistols, with which they were armed. The two Policemen

日本海军陆战队成员与上海公共租界工部局警务处警员之间的事件。
--------------------------------------------------

先生：

    1941年2月17日凌晨3时50分，上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）第四营的普赖斯（Price）中尉会同中央巡捕房411号和561号警员来到巡捕房，报告称这两名中央巡捕房警员被两名身穿日本海军陆战队制服的日本男子缴械并带走。

    经后续调查，查明情况如下。

    1941年2月17日凌晨2时45分，中央巡捕房411号和531号警员正在宜昌路桥3号岗哨执勤。突然，他们听到戈登路上传来喊叫声，经查看，发现一辆车牌号为21的日本海军陆战队机动车熄灯停在戈登路靠近宜昌路处。当他们走近时，车辆开始向他们移动。然而，当汽车到达中央巡捕房警员面前时，两名日本男子下车，开始用日语与警察交谈。这两名日本人均身穿日本海军陆战队制服，情绪显得激动，交谈几秒钟后，突然用手枪枪托袭击两名中央巡捕房警员的面部和头部。两名警察

struggle, their pistol lanyards were broken and both of

Gordon Roads, the motor car swung around and returned
to where the C.P.Cs were standing.
    The two Japanese again alighted and pointing their
pistols at the two Policemen ordered them into the
motor car.
    The two C.P.Cs were forced to sit in the rear seat
of the motor car and whilst one Japanese guarded them

    Almost immediately, they were approached by another
member of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, who spoke to
the two men. A few minutes later, the two men returned
the C.P.Cs' pistols and caps and told them to go.

1940年5月1日下午5时10分，接获顺泰路堆栈工部局负责人霍尔特（Holt）先生电话通知，称当日午后3时30分，有四名工部局苦力在极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）与小渡浜路（Crossing Road）交叉口以东、金西尔路（Kinseer Road）中段附近清理一条小河沟时，被日本宪兵和上海市政府警察逮捕。

副巡官755号横泽（H. Yokosawa）与本人随即前往极司菲尔路92号上海市政府警察第一大队。因已逾办公时间，未能晤见任何负责人。从卫兵处获悉，这些苦力系由西区联络官北冈（Kitaoka）先生因语言误会而带入，并于当日下午5时30分获释。

霍尔特先生进一步指出，数周前曾发生类似事件，当时有四枚徽章被没收，他请求警方调查该等徽章之下落。本人将于1940年5月2日办公时间内再次拜访北冈先生。

pass, and showed same to the members of the patrol, but this
act failed to produce the result desired, as a member of the
patrol slapped the detective upon the face, and released the
prisoner.

Yulin Road Station,
REPORT
Date August 31, 1939
Subject S.M.C/P... Coolie assaulted by Japanese Military, at Baikal
Road.
Made by J.I.Ross Forwarded by (Signature)

Sir:
At 4.40 p.m. 31/8/39, Inspector Pavlovsky, S.M.C./
P...D. antung road depot, brought to Yulin Road station
coolie No. 1233 Lee Tsai Yee (李蔡二) who complained
that he had been the victim of an assault by the Japanese
Military, whilst performing his departmental duties,
at Baikal Road.

Enquiries by C.D.C. 321 and the undersigned ascer-
tained the following:- At about 3 p.m. 31/8/39, the
coolie Lee Tsai Yee was engaged sweeping the highway
and footpaths at Baikal Road near Liaoyang Road. At the
time two Japanese soldiers were engaged at the same
location repairing the bamboo fencing surrounding a
building which the Military has occupied.

When Lee Tsai Yee was engaged sweeping the footpath
he accidentally touched the foot of one of the soldiers
with the brush, and this resulted in the soldier slapping
the coolie's face and knocking him to the ground. When
the coolie was lying upon the footpath the soldier
then kicked him on the chin.

The coolie, Lee Tsai Yee, was sent to the Yangtsepoo
Hospital for medical examination, and the following cer-
tificate was issued regarding his injuries:-
"Laceration of lower jaw. Not serious. Not detained."

The detectives conducted discreet enquiries in the
vicinity where the assault occurred, but were unable
to locate any eye-witnesses of the affair.

A written statement has been prepared by Lee Tsai
Yee, and a translated copy of this is attached.

先生：
1939年8月31日下午4时40分，隶属于工部局/公共工程部安东路堆栈的帕夫洛夫斯基（Pavlovsky）巡官，将第1233号苦力李蔡二（Lee Tsai Yee）带至榆林路捕房，该苦力诉称其在贝加尔路（Baikal Road）执行部门职务时，成为日本军队袭击的受害者。

经刑事侦缉警员第321号及具报人查询，查明情况如下：1939年8月31日下午3时许，苦力李蔡二正在辽阳路附近的贝加尔路清扫马路及人行道。当时，两名日本士兵正在同一地点修理围绕着一栋被军队占领的建筑物的竹篱笆。

当李蔡二清扫人行道时，他的扫帚不慎碰到了其中一名士兵的脚，导致该士兵打了苦力一记耳光并将其击倒在地。当苦力躺在人行道上时，该士兵又踢了他的下巴。

苦力李蔡二被送往杨树浦医院接受体检，并就其伤情出具了以下证明：
“下颚撕裂伤。不严重。不予留院。”

侦探们在袭击发生地附近进行了谨慎的调查，但未能找到任何目击者。

李蔡二已准备了一份书面陈述，附有其译本。

Sir,
At 10 ... 17-8-1939, Inspector Pavlovsky, attached to the S.M.C./P.W.D. Antung Road Depot, brought to Yulin Road Station Foreman No. 8 Mei Kying Sung (梅金生) and Coolie No. 1231 Lee Lung Chong, (李成昌) and reported that the latter had been assaulted by a Japanese at Pingliang Road, whilst performing his duty.

Enquiries by Det. Sub-Inspector Lee Kee Tong and the undersigned ascertained the following:-

At about 9.15 a.m. 17-8-1939, coolie No. 1231 Lee Lung Chong was engaged sweeping the highway at Pingliang Road near Jansen Road, in the vicinity of the Japanese Gendarmerie Station, at 250 Pingliang Road. At this juncture an unknown Japanese wearing khaki coloured military type uniform left the building, called the coolie, and pointed out that some ashes and waste paper was lying alongside a bamboo fence at the side of the station. He slapped and kicked the coolie a number of times, and forced him to remove the rubbish.

The coolie reported the occurrence to Foreman No. 8 Mei Kying Sung, who was in the vicinity supervising the work of the sweepers, and who witnessed the assault. The two attended the Antung Road Depot and lodged a complaint.

Written statements regarding the incident were prepared by the coolie and the foreman and translated copies of these are attached.

The coolie did not sustain injury of sufficient seriousness to justify medical treatment.

I am, Sir,

1939年6月19日上午11时10分，一辆公共工程部卡车将公共工程部垃圾苦力第1238号余灶基（Yue Tsau Kyi）；41岁，海门籍，无编号房屋，居住于阜宁路；带至捕房，该人左腿受伤，据称是被一名日本士兵用刺刀刺伤所致。

此人被送往警察医院，医生出具证明如下：
“兹报告公共工程部苦力1238号今日入院治疗，因其左大腿有切割伤。”

经侦探花轮（Hanawa）、刑事侦缉警员第334号及具报人查询，获悉1939年6月19日上午9时40分许，伤者正在兆丰路清理瓦砾，并将收集到的大量垃圾抛掷在兆丰路与百老汇路（Broadway）拐角处的拆除房产上，位置在兆丰路上百老汇路以北约10码处。当时，据病人称，他在瓦砾中发现一个烟头，便弯腰去捡，但就在那时，一名日本士兵走近他，在用日语说话（他听不懂）后，用刺刀刺了他，随即离去。

他随后查看伤势，走到马路对面，用一块布包扎伤口。他在那里停留了一段时间，之后，由于临近上午11时，所有苦力必须到路边路（Wayside Road）与百老汇东路拐角处报到，他便跛行前往该处，并向其工头报告了此事

hawker's stall on the corner of Broadway East and Chaoufoong

out ground. Suddenly I saw two Japanese soldiers wearing

to west. One of the soldiers walked to the burnt-out ground

the side of a telegraph pole on the west side of Chaoufoong
Road. I also saw him lifting up his trouser leg and inspecting
his wounded leg. I watched him for a few minutes. He walked
away in an easterly direction towards Broadway East.

At 6 a.m. on 19-6-39, I was detailed to clean Broadway
East, Kent and Chaoufoong Roads.
At about 9.40 a.m. same date, I threw a quantity of
garbage collected into a small alleyway adjacent to a piece
of burned-out ground on Chaoufoong Road. At that time, I
noticed a cigarette end on the ground. When I was in the
act of picking the cigarette end up I was observed by a
Japanese soldier who talked to me in Japanese which I did
not understand. He then stabbed me on my left thigh with
his bayonet which was affixed to a rifle.
As my injured left leg was bleeding badly, I went to
the side of the road and wrapped my wound with a length
of cloth.
At 11 a.m. even date, being the time to report our
work, I walked to the corner of Broadway East and Wayside
Road, where I reported the occurrence to the sub-foreman
named Hong. I was then sent to the Police Station from there
I was conveyed to a hospital for treatment.
I should not be able to recognize the soldier if I see
him again.

Made by D.S. Bretherton Forwarded by B. Palmer, Inspt.

Sir,

I have to report, that at 10.20 p.m. on the 18-5-39
whilst pursuing enquiries with reference to F.l.h. 144/39
T'poo, I had occasion to ride in this station m/car Lic.
No. 1324 accompanied by one prisoner; C.D.C. 163 and C.D.S.
170 in Tientsin and Kay Roads. Seated beside the chauffeur,
King Ho Heng (王阿根), No. 46, we stopped the vehicle at the
intersection of Peshien and Glen Roads, where there is posted
a sentries, members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party.
I indicated to the sentry nearest to me, i.e. the rear side
of the vehicle, that we were Police and in response he waved
us on. The chauffeur not yet having set the vehicle in
motion, the sentry posted on the other side of the inter-
section, i.e. offside of the vehicle, shouted intimating for
us not to start. Coming over to the offside near the
chauffeur the Sentry pointed to the vehicle's head lamp and
struck the chauffeur on the face for no apparent reason.
The chauffeur switched the vehicle lights on and off,
in an endeavour to demonstrate to the sentry that they were
quite in order, this resulted in a second blow to the
chauffeur's face by the sentry. He then enquired of the
vehicle passengers and when informed by me, speaking in
English, that they were detectives and a prisoner he allowed
the vehicle to proceed.

It is well to mention, that no Japanese Police Officer
accompanied us at the time, those on duty being otherwise
engaged. Also, that the vehicle lighting was quite in order,
I having examined it immediately after. The chauffeur
suffered no untoward injury, and does not wish to make a
statement.

H. Bretherton

先生，

谨此报告，1939年5月18日晚上10时20分，我在就F.l.h. 144/39 T'poo一案进行调查时，有机会乘坐本局牌照号为1324的机动车，车上有一名囚犯，以及C.D.C. 163和C.D.S. 170，行驶在天津路和凯路。坐在司机金阿根（King Ho Heng，编号46）旁边，我们在北四川路和格兰路（Glen Roads）的交叉口停下车，那里驻有日本海军陆战队的哨兵。
我向离我最近的哨兵，即车辆后侧的哨兵，示意我们是警察，作为回应，他挥手让我们通过。由于司机尚未启动车辆，位于交叉口另一侧，即车辆外侧的哨兵大声喊叫，示意我们不要启动。该哨兵走到靠近司机的车辆外侧，指着车辆的前大灯，并无端击打司机的面部。
司机开关车辆灯光，试图向哨兵证明灯光完好无损，这导致哨兵第二次击打司机的面部。随后他询问车内乘客，当我用英语告诉他他们是侦探和一名囚犯时，他允许车辆通行。

值得一提的是，当时没有日本警官陪同我们，值勤人员另有任务。此外，车辆灯光完好无损，我在事后立即进行了检查。司机未受严重伤害，且不希望做供词。

I beg to report that I was transferred to Gordon Road
Station from Bayside on 21.3.42. I and S.P.C. 189 put our
belongings in middle Van No. 10255 and set out for Gordon
Road Station.

At 9.45 a.m. at the Garden Bridge we were stopped by the
Japanese Naval sentry who asked for a pass. We replied that we
had no pass and rang up called to S.P.C. 816 to explain the
matter. Before he arrived with the sentry but the sentry
refused to let us pass and took the chauffeur and took us to
the Japanese Headquarters at Hankou Road.

We did not take any other action.

We were kept sitting in the Van at Japanese Headquarters and
later a Japanese sub-inspector attached to Bayside Station
came to the place and spoke to the Japanese officers. Whilst
the sub-inspector was talking a Japanese Superintendent arrived
went inside the building. A short time later the sub-inspector
came out and told the chauffeur to leave the van and took we two
police officers and the Chinese chauffeur to Hongkew Station in
Bayside Station car.

This is my true statement.

(Sd) Karpal Singh

REPORT
Date March 21, 1939.
Subject Re detention of police man by the Japanese Sentry.
Made by J.P.C. 216.

Sir,
I beg to report that at about 10 a.m. 21/3/39 while I was on duty on Garden Bridge, I observed Police Van Lic. No. 7 was proceeding from South to East on Broadway. The Van was stopped by the Japanese Sentry about to cross the bridge by the members of the Japanese Consular Police and the Japanese Sentry on duty at the Bridge. The Van was examined by the Sentry and found that the Van was loaded with furnitures and S.P.C. and C.P.C. board on the Van. At this juncture, F.S.98 was approaching to me and requesting that I ask the sentries that the van be allowed to pass over the bridge. The sentry, however, said that as the driver had no pass to transport goods he could not allow him to proceed.

At this time the foreign sergeant asked me why the van could not go and told the chauffeur to drive on, in a very excited tone. The driver attempted to start the engine when he was again stopped by the sentry, who was standing about 15 yards ahead of the car. The car was then again thoroughly reexamined and then taken to the J.N.L.P. Headquarters.

Your Obedient servant,

Sgd. S. Iijim
J.P.C.216.

先生，
谨此报告，1939年3月21日上午10时许，当我在外白渡桥执勤时，我观察到牌照号为7号的警车正沿百老汇路（Broadway）由南向东行驶。该货车在即将过桥时被日本领事馆警察成员及在桥上执勤的日本哨兵拦停。哨兵检查了货车，发现车上装载着家具，且有印籍巡捕（S.P.C.）和华捕（C.P.C.）在车上。此时，外籍警员（F.S.）编号98向我走来，请求我询问哨兵是否允许该货车过桥。然而，哨兵称由于司机没有货物运输通行证，故不能允许其通行。

此时，外籍警长问我货车为何不能通行，并以非常激动的语气告诉司机继续开车。司机试图启动引擎，但再次被站在车前约15码处的哨兵拦下。随后该车再次受到彻底复查，然后被带往日本海军陆战队警察局（J.N.L.P.）总部。

您顺从的仆人，

Enquiries made by S.I. Vasudevan, I.P., India and J.R.C. 1st Engineer ascertained that at about 10.30a.m. 21/8/38, the truck was driven into an unmetalled lane leading from Reclamation Road, East of Junction Road, where the R.V.P. have been depositing soil for the past 3 months.

On approaching the rear of Nos. 104, 105 & 106 Reclamation Road, occupied by the Eastern Branch of the Japanese Military Special Service Section, the driver observed two uniformed white lights rocks, which were placed on either side of the above house.

He stopped his truck, and alighting from same went down the truck path to them to ask what was the matter.

After depositing the soil, the military authorities took possession of the truck and ordered the driver and the two coolies to go with them to their headquarters.

Sir,
I beg to report that at 8.10 a.m. on 27/10/38 the
following occurrence took place on the Garden Bridge whilst
I was performing my duty.
At about 8.10 a.m. a Japanese Consular policeman
approached me and requested me to report the following
incident to the Station, stating that a bus No.20576,
driven by a Foreign driver and carrying foreign female
passengers and about 4 children just passed over the Bridge,
and one foreign boy who was sitting in the rear of the bus
had stuck his head out of the window and showed him and the
Japanese Marine Sentry his tongue. I was standing on the
west side of the bridge and about 15 yards north at the
time of the incident, therefore not witnessing same, I then
explained to him that I would investigate on the returning
of the bus.
At 9.30 a.m. a bus licence No.20576 crossed the bridge
from south to north and was ordered to stop by Japanese
sentry, I then ascertained that the bus belongs to the
S.M.Police and there were 4 lady passengers, I was requested
by the Warrant officer of the Japanese Marines to translate
to the ladies that a small foreign boy had shown his tongue
to the Japanese Consular Policeman and the sentry at 8.10 a.m.
this morning, so they are going to take them and the bus to
the Headquarters of the Japanese Naval Landing Party (Nannen
Road) for investigation. A Japanese Warrant officer boarded
the bus and the bus proceeded North of the Creek, I then
informed the incident to the Station through a public tele-
phone.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
Sd. E.Kurlansky

D.C. "D" Office,
October 7th, 1938.

Chauffeur assaulted by Japanese Consular
Policeman on Szechuen Road Bridge.

Sir,

At 8.45 a.m. October 7th, 1938, I was proceeding North
over Szechuen Road Bridge in m/c 10440, driven by S. M. P.
chauffeur No. 7 Li Tuh Piao driving permit No. 13227. Also
seated in the car were D.S.I. Suhoff (W) and clerk Ku Hsing
Chu. On approaching the crown of the bridge the car was
slowed to almost a standstill while clerk Ku displayed his pass
to the Japanese uniform men on duty there. As the car slowly
passed, a small Japanese dressed in Consular Police uniform
wearing high boots and one star on his shoulder straps,
suddenly shouted which brought the car to a halt. This petty
official then jumped on to the running board, reached over
and attempted to strike the chauffeur in the face, apparently
for failing to display his pass promptly, no blows actually
touched the chauffeur's face as he effectively warded them off.
Fortunately I was not in a position where I could take quick
protective action and thereby create an incident. This display
of bullying officiousness on the part of the Consular Policeman
was entirely unwarranted. The motor car bore a signed S.M.P.
label pasted on the windscreen, and the chauffeur was dressed
in police chauffeurs' uniform and cap. In view of which, the
action can only be construed as an unfriendly and insulting
gesture.

J.P.C. 225 on duty at the bridge witnessed the incident,
but owing to its brevity, his services were not required. He
could no doubt identify the official concerned.

D. O. "D" Division.

D.C. (Divisions).

“D”分区副督察办公室，
1938年10月7日。

司机在四川路桥遭日本领事馆警察殴打。

先生，

1938年10月7日上午8时45分，我乘坐10440号机动车
由北向南驶过四川路桥，该车由上海公共租界工部局警务处
7号司机李土彪（Li Tuh Piao，驾驶证号13227）驾驶。
车内还坐着 Suhoff 侦探副督察（白人）及职员 Ku Hsing Chu。
当车辆接近桥顶时，车速减慢至几乎停止，此时职员 Ku
向在那里执勤的日本制服人员出示通行证。当车辆缓慢通过时，
一名身穿领事馆警察制服、脚蹬高筒靴、肩章上有一颗星的小个子日本人
突然大喊，导致车辆停下。这名小官员随即跳上脚踏板，
伸手试图击打司机的面部，显然是因为司机未能及时出示通行证，
但由于司机有效格挡，拳头并未实际击中司机面部。
幸好我当时所处位置不便迅速采取保护行动，从而避免引发事端。
这名领事馆警察表现出的仗势欺人的傲慢行为完全毫无道理。
机动车挡风玻璃上贴有签名的上海公共租界工部局标签，
司机身着警务司机制服并佩戴帽子。鉴于此，
该行为只能被解读为一种不友好且带有侮辱性的姿态。

当时在桥上执勤的225号巡佐 J.P.C. 目睹了这一事件，
但由于事件持续时间极短，无需其介入。他无疑能指认
涉事官员。

各分区副督察。

OBJECT IN POLICING
HONGKEW BRIDGES

Japanese Consular Men
There To Help Return
To Peace Conditions

Stationing of Japanese consular
policemen since July 1, on Garden
and Szechuen Road bridges were
effected so as to "lead back to peace
the conditions in Shanghai," a
spokesman for the Japanese Navy
said yesterday.
The policemen, he continued, were
detailed to assist bluejackets in inspecting the transit passes of Chinese and the movement of goods
from Yangtzepoo and Hongkew and
also to carry out general police duties.
"The purpose of this step," the
spokesman explained," was to prevent misunderstandings arising from
language difficulties and differences
in customs between third-party nationals and the sentries charged with
inspecting goods. It was also intended to give a more peaceful impression to the persons coming into
contact with the official in charge.
"Consequently, insofar as the execution of their duties, which have
been entrusted to them by the naval
authorities, they are subject to
orders from the commandant of the
Japanese Special Naval Landing
Party.
"These consular policemen are
consequently acting in compliance
to the instructions of the officer in
charge of the defence of the Japanese sector. They are acting as assistants to the sentries and their
duties are as important as those
whom they represent."
pages.zh:
虹口桥梁警务之目的

日本领事馆人员
在此协助恢复
和平状态

日本海军发言人昨日表示，自7月1日起在日本领事馆警察部署于花园桥及四川路桥，旨在“使上海的局势回归和平”。
他继续说道，这些警察被指派协助水兵检查中国人的通行证以及来自杨树浦和虹口的货物流动，并执行一般警务职责。
该发言人解释说：“此举的目的是防止因语言障碍及风俗习惯差异，导致第三方国籍人士与负责检查货物的哨兵之间产生误解。这也意在给与负责官员接触的人员留下更为平和的印象。”
“因此，就其受海军当局委托执行的职务而言，他们须服从日本特别海军陆战队指挥官的命令。”
“因此，这些领事警察是遵照负责日占区防御的军官的指令行事。他们作为哨兵的助手，其职责与他们所代表的人员同样重要。”

pages.en:
Police Jurisdiction In Hongkew
The Japanese authorities will
retain police jurisdiction over that
section of Hongkew which has
recently be thrown open to the
public, it was reported today. Al-
though more than 20 Chinese con-
stables of the S.M.P. have been
detailed north of the Creek to
assist the Japanese police "as an
experiment," this should not give
rise to the expectation that the
Japanese authorities would relin-
quish their police rights over the
area, it was reported.
The resumption of tram services
north of the creek is also another
moot question under discussion
between the Japanese and the other
foreign consular authorities. The
Japanese have argued that if the
Chinese were to be permitted too
free a movement in Hongkew and
in the Eastern District, the "radical
elements" might create distur-
bances, hence the resumption of
tram services in gradual stages.
pages.zh:
虹口的警务管辖权

据报道，日本当局将保留对最近向公众开放的虹口区域的警务管辖权。尽管已有超过20名工部局警务处的中国巡捕被派往苏州河以北，以“试验性”方式协助日本警察，但据报道，这不应让人产生日本当局会放弃对该地区警务权利的期望。

恢复苏州河以北的电车服务也是日本与其他外国领事当局之间讨论的另一个争议问题。日方辩称，如果允许中国人在虹口和东区过于自由地活动，“激进分子”可能会制造骚乱，因此电车服务的恢复将分阶段逐步进行。

Subject Incident between Japanese and ricksha coolie on Nanking Road near
Shanse Road involving C.P.C.1667, who was assaulted by a Japanese.
Made by D.S. Macadie Forwarded by

Sir,
At 10.35 p.m. 22-2-38, a motor car, S.D.F. Licence No.196,
was proceeding eastwards along Nanking Road about thirty yards
west of Shanse Road when a ricksha, S.M.C. Licence No.4990, pulled
by Wong Gee Ji (王其吉), aged 22, native of Kompo, residing un-
numbered straw hut off Singapore Road, permit No.19557, dashed
across the road from South to North. This necessitated the motor
car pulling up sharply to avoid a collision. The driver of the
car a Japanese in military uniform got out and attempted to seize
the ricksha coolie who however ran away. At this juncture C.P.C.
1667 on patrol came on the scene when the Japanese in uniform
who had already removed the enamel licence plate of the ricksha
on the mudguard told him in Chinese to take off the ordinary
licence plate. The C.P.C. observed that the plate had already
been removed from the back of the ricksha and replied to that
effect. The Japanese driver then seized the C.P.C. by the arm
and started to pull him towards the car. At this stage the four
Japanese civilian occupants of the car alighted and pulled the
driver away. The car then drove off.
No collision actually took place.
Statements of C.P.C.1667 and ricksha coolie attached.

R.W. Mac adie
D.S. 368

Senior Detective i/c.

D.D.O. "A" Division.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS

Deng Tsung Ping, C.P.C.1667, attached Louss,
taken by me self,
Louss Station on the 22-2-38, and transcribed by Clerk in Pang Yeo.

At 7.00 p.m. 22-2-38 I was detailed by the foreign
inspector to patrol the 4th section of Nanking Road.
Whilst patrolling on Nanking Road near Thihli Road,
I heard a sudden noise of a motor car brakes being applied. I
immediately went to the place where I saw a black sedan motor
car, S.D.F. Licence No.196, facing east on Nanking Road about
30 yards west of Shanse Road, and also a public ricksha with
its shafts upwards and facing south on the left kerb of the
road. A Japanese soldier in brown uniform using a short sword
was seen removing the enamel licence plate away from the public
ricksha and the ricksha coolie had already ran away.
I approached him and enquired of him what had happened.
He told me in Chinese to take the licence plate down from the
ricksha, to which I replied that the licence plate had already
been removed. The said Japanese soldier then siezed me by my
left arm and attempted to strike me but he was however pulled
away by four other Japanese in civilian clothing. All of them
then boarded the motor car and drove away in a westerly direc-
tion. After which the ricksha coolie came whom I brought to-
gether with the public ricksha to the Charge Room.
The above is my true statement.
(Signed) Deng Tsung Ping C.P.C.1667.

邓宗平（Deng Tsung Ping），华捕1667号，隶属老闸捕房，
由我本人于1938年2月22日在老闸捕房录取，
由书记员潘耀（Pang Yeo，音译）转录。

1938年2月22日晚上7时（注：此处时间与上文10:35不符，依原文翻译），我被外籍督察指派巡逻南京路第四段。
当在南京路近铁力路（Thihli Road，音译，即浙江中路或附近小路）巡逻时，我听到突然的汽车刹车声。我立即前往该处，看到一辆黑色轿车，车牌号S.D.F. 196，车头朝东停在南京路上，位于山西路以西约30码处，还有一辆公共人力车车把朝天，车头朝南停在道路左侧路缘石旁。一名身穿棕色制服的日本士兵正用短剑将公共人力车上的搪瓷牌照撬下，人力车夫已经逃跑。
我走近他，询问发生了什么事。他用中文让我把人力车上的牌照取下，我回答说牌照已经被取下了。该名日本士兵随即抓住我的左臂并试图殴打我，但被另外四名身穿便服的日本人拉开。随后他们全部登上汽车，向西方向驶离。之后人力车夫回来，我将他和人力车一起带回了拘留室。
以上是我的真实陈述。
（签名）邓宗平 华捕1667号。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Weng Gee Si, a public ricksha coolie, age 27,
residing unnumbered straw hut
native of Kempe, off Singapore Rd, taken by me C.D.C.42,
at Louza Station, on the 22-2-38, and translated by Clerk Li Pang Yao.

At 10.35 p.m. 22-2-38, whilst plying public ricksha, S.M.C.
license No.4990, on Nanking Road about 30 yards west of Shanse Rd,
I dashed across Nanking Road from South to North when a motor car,
S.D.F. License No.196, which was proceeding from East to West on
Nanking Road, suddenly approached but the motor car was able to
stop in order to avoid collision with my ricksha. In the motor car
were one Japanese soldier in uniform and four civilian Japanese.
The uniformed Japanese then alighted from the motor car and tried
to sieze and assault me. I abandoned the ricksha and ran away from
the scene. About 10 minutes later I returned to the place where
I found the said motor car had driven away and the enamel license
plate of my ricksha had been removed away by someone. A C.P.C. was
then on the scene who later brought me together with the ricksha
to this station.

The above is my true statement.

(Crossed) Weng Gee Si.

1938年2月22日晚上10时35分，当我驾驶车牌号为S.M.C. 4990的公共人力车在南京路上运营，行至山西路以西约30码处时，我从南向北横穿南京路，此时一辆车牌号为S.D.F. 196的汽车正沿南京路从东向西行驶，突然逼近，但汽车得以停下，以避免与我的车相撞。车内有一名身穿军服的日本士兵和四名日本平民。那名身穿军服的日本人随后下车，试图抓住并殴打我。我弃车逃离现场。大约10分钟后我回到原地，发现那辆汽车已经驶离，我车上的搪瓷牌照已被某人拆走。当时有一名华捕在现场，他后来将我和人力车一起带到了本捕房。

REPORT
Date Feb. 20, 19 38.

Subject Arrest of two Chinese private watchmen employed at the Derring
partments, Tsungming Road by Japanese Military.

Made by Inspector Trodd Forwarded by Inspector [Signature]

Sir,

I beg to report that at 2.45 p.m. 20-2-38 six members of the
Japanese Military entered the Derring Apartments, Tsungming Road,
and informed the Chinese watchmen that they were looking for
seven electric motors which had been stolen from the Bridge
House. They then searched the premises and finding three motors
in the boiler room, asked for the remainder but were informed
by the watchmen that they had been previously stolen by looters
from the Bridge House and not recovered. Seven of the looters
had been arrested and charged by the Police during December
1937 and the three found on the premises had been removed from
the Bridge House, in the presence of the Police, for safe
custody. The Japanese were apparently not satisfied with their
story and, taking the three electric motors, requested the two
watchmen whose names are Wong Dee Zung (王殿正) and Zau Fung
Tong (趙風桐) to accompany them to the "Asia Hotel", Tiendong
Road, the Headquarters of the Japanese Military Police.

Upon arrival there they were again interrogated regarding
the four missing motors and reiterated their previous explanation
with the added information that one Fu Ping (傅平), their No.
1 watchman, and the Police, knew the whole facts of the case.

Wong Dee Zung was released at 3.10 p.m. and told to request
"Fu Ping" to go to the Asia Hotel and verify their statements
pending which Zau Fung Tong would be detained.

At 4 p.m. Wong Dee Zung accompanied by "Fu Ping", came to
this station and reported the occurrence whereupon the undersigned
and J.D.C. 132 immediately instituted enquiries and ascertained
that the information as given by the watchmen was true and
forms the subject of F.I.R. 8347/38 of Hongkew Station, conducted
by P.C. 216.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 21 FEB. 1938）

日期 1938年2月20日。

事由：日本军方逮捕两名受雇于崇明路 Derring 公寓（音译）的中国私人更夫。

呈报人：特罗德（Trodd）巡官 转呈人：[签名] 巡官

先生，

谨此报告，1938年2月20日下午2时45分，六名日本军人进入崇明路 Derring 公寓，告知中国更夫他们正在寻找从 Bridge House（音译）被盗的七台电动机。随后他们搜查了该处所，并在锅炉房发现了三台电动机，遂询问其余电动机的下落，但更夫告知他们，其余电动机此前已被来自 Bridge House 的劫掠者盗走，且未追回。1937年12月期间，警方已逮捕并起诉了七名劫掠者，而在该处所发现的三台电动机已在警方在场见证下从 Bridge House 移出，以便妥善保管。日本人显然对他们的解释不满意，拿走了这三台电动机，并要求两名更夫——王殿正（Wong Dee Zung）和趙風桐（Zau Fung Tong）——陪同他们前往天潼路“亚洲饭店”，即日本宪兵队总部。

抵达那里后，他们就四台失踪的电动机再次对他们进行审问，两人重申了先前的解释，并补充说明他们的头号更夫傅平（Fu Ping）以及警方知晓案件的全部事实。

王殿正于下午3时10分获释，并被告知请“傅平”前往亚洲饭店以证实他们的陈述，在此期间趙風桐将被拘留。

下午4时，王殿正在“傅平”的陪同下来到本巡捕房报告此事，随后卑职与 J.D.C. 132 立即展开调查，并查明更夫所提供的信息属实，该事项构成虹口巡捕房由警员 216 号处理的第 8347/38 号首次调查报告（F.I.R.）的主题。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特别支部 1938年2月21日）
（批：Des B / SAR / 242 / S.1 / C. 3/2）

keep out of the "Prohibited area". At 4.50.p.m. on arrival of
Supt: Sinclair, D.O. "D" S.I. Moore was released. For further

Sir,
        I beg to report that at 12 noon to-day C.P.W. 1100 was
brought to this station by J.D.S. 42, the Japanese military
police having previously telephoned that they were ready to
release this man.
        From brief questioning at the station the impression
was received that the assurance given to J.D.S. 42 yesterday
by the Japanese military police that this sixty-three year-old
Police watchman would not be harmed had, surprisingly enough,
not been scrupulously honoured and, on the instructions of the
D.D.O., C.P.W. 1100 was removed to Police headquarters in order
that a detailed statement regarding his experience might be
taken from him.
        From what the watchman told detectives at this station
it was gathered that the three main lines of questioning pursued
by the Japanese were his early omission to mention the presence
of his wife and her periodical trips to Shanghai, the names of
the foreign and Chinese staff of the China Soap Co., and the
final destination of stocks removed from the firm's Yangtzepoo
premises by lighter to Shanghai. The Japanese apparently
found it difficult to believe in the watchman's natural ignorance
upon this last point and '' was probably this that resulted in
his being detained for so long a period (7.30 a.m. 12/10/37
to 12 noon 13/10/37).
        C.P.W. 1100 has been left at Central and Mr. Harper,
manager of the China Soap Co., does not wish him to return to
this area.

                                        I am, Sir,
                                        Yours obediently,

        通过在巡捕房的简短讯问，得到的印象是，日本宪兵队昨天向日本警佐 42 号作出的保证——即这名六十三岁的警务更夫不会受到伤害——令人惊讶地并未得到严格遵守，根据副分区警官的指示，中国肥皂公司警员 1100 号被移送至警察总局，以便从他那里获取关于其经历的详细陈述。
        根据该更夫告诉本巡捕房侦探的内容，获悉日本方面追问的三个主要方向是：他早期未提及妻子的存在及其定期往返上海的情况；中国肥皂公司的外籍和华籍职员名单；以及该公司杨树浦厂址通过驳船运往上海的库存货物的最终目的地。日本人似乎难以相信更夫在这最后一点上的自然无知，这很可能导致他被拘留如此长的时间（1937年10月12日上午7时30分至1937年10月13日中午12时）。
        中国肥皂公司警员 1100 号已被留在中央巡捕房，中国肥皂公司经理哈珀（Harper）先生不希望他返回该地区。

My name is Wong Kwong Zung, age 63, native of Shantung,

My wife left the factory at 4 p.m. October 11, by the

the address of the office of the company. I replied that the
products consisted of soap, butter and glycerine and the Russian

two truck loads of large wooden cases, contents of which were
unknown to them. Simultaneously to this report being made
Private watchman Basam Singh, employed at the No.1 Wing On
Cotton Mill, Seoul road, came to station and reported that
earlier that morning Japanese military had removed several
truck loads of cotton cloth and cotton wool. In both instances
no action could be taken, and this report is made for record

At 9-15 a.m. 12/10/37, Mr. Fletcher of the China Soap Co.
came to station and reported that approximately 7-30 that

杨树浦
1937年10月13日。

截至1937年10月13日上午6时的24小时内，杨树浦地区的中日敌对行动情况。
D.S.I. Crighton。[签名] 主管警官。

先生，
          谨此报告，自1937年10月12日清晨起，日本军舰和轰炸机持续轰炸与本巡捕房辖区及榆林路（Yulin roads）地区直接相对的浦东地区。作为回应，偶尔能听到机枪射击声，无疑是对准飞机的，这些飞机有时飞得很低。
          1937年10月12日上午10时40分，两名私人印度看门人，即哈纳姆（Harnam）和萨汉·辛格（Saham Singh），均受雇于杨树浦路1616号永安公司（Wing On Company）仓库，来到本巡捕房报告称，在他们到达巡捕房之前，日本军方已运走五卡车棉纱，以及两卡车大型木箱，箱内物品他们不知情。与此同时，受雇于首尔路（Seoul road）永安第一棉纺织厂（No.1 Wing On Cotton Mill）的私人看门人巴萨姆·辛格（Basam Singh）也来到巡捕房报告称，当天早晨早些时候，日本军方已运走数卡车棉布和棉花。在这两起事件中，均无法采取行动，本报告仅作记录之用。
          1937年10月12日上午9时15分，中国肥皂公司（China Soap Co.）的弗莱彻（Fletcher）先生来到巡捕房报告称，约在当天上午7时30分，日本军方当局进入该处所并逮捕了他的中国看门人。此事已由 D.E. Blake 另行专题报告。
          1937年10月12日整夜，未发生任何显著事件。

          先生，
          您忠顺的仆人，
          [签名]
